findings.title: Blocked email matching is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using the raw email string exactly as submitted by the user, with no downcasing/normalization. Since the User model does not appear to normalize/downcase the email before validation runs (normalization such as Email.downcase is only used elsewhere, e.g. find_by_username_or_email), an attacker can trivially bypass a block entry such as 'spam@evil.com' by signing up with 'Spam@Evil.com' or any different casing. This defeats the entire purpose of the blocked-email feature.

findings.title: Non-atomic counter update is subject to lost updates under concurrency
findings.body: should_block? loads the record, then does `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` as separate read-then-write steps. If two signup/validation requests hit the same blocked email concurrently, both will read the same match_count, increment it independently, and the last writer wins, silently losing one of the increments. For a feature meant to produce accurate abuse statistics, this is a legitimate data-integrity concern that should use an atomic UPDATE (e.g. `update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', ...])`).

findings.title: Email validation (and its side effects) runs twice per signup, double-counting blocked-email statistics
findings.body: In `create`, `user.valid?` is called first (left operand of `&&`, so it always executes regardless of `call_discourse_hub?`), and later `user.save` triggers the full validation chain again. Because `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which has the side effect of incrementing `match_count` and updating `last_match_at` on every invocation, a single signup attempt against a blocked email will increment the counter twice instead of once, corrupting the abuse statistics the feature is meant to produce.

findings.title: No test coverage for the migrated whitelist/blacklist domain validation logic
findings.body: The whitelist/blacklist domain-restriction logic (`email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist`) was moved out of User#email_validator into this new EmailValidator class, but spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb only exercises the new 'blocked email' branch (lines 9-21) via stubbed BlockedEmail.should_block?. There is no test verifying that the whitelist/blacklist branches still add the `not_allowed` error correctly after being refactored into this class, so a regression in that previously-tested behavior would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Structured per-field errors and submitted values now exposed on signup failure, enabling account/field enumeration
findings.body: The `create` action's failure response now includes `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` in addition to the message. Previously only a combined message string was returned. Returning a machine-readable mapping of which specific field failed (e.g. `errors: {email: ["has already been taken"]}`) makes it trivial for an automated script to enumerate which emails/usernames are already registered or blocked, which is a stronger enumeration primitive than the prior free-text message.

findings.title: rejectedEmails permanently blacklists an email for any email-related server error, not just blocked/invalid emails
findings.body: In createAccount's failure handler, any response where `result.errors.email` is present causes `result.values.email` to be pushed into `rejectedEmails` forever (for the life of the controller instance), regardless of the actual reason for the email error (blocked email, domain restriction, transient server/DiscourseHub failure, etc.). Once added, `emailValidation` will always report that email as failed even if the underlying condition was transient or already resolved (e.g. a temporary DiscourseHub timeout), preventing the user from ever resubmitting that same email in the same session without reloading the page.
